sources.title: WBPCB EMIS citizen water-quality portal: 41 stations, quarterly sampling 2010-2026, high and low tide pairs
sources.license: WBPCB citizen data portal, cited with attribution

conventions.tidal_phase: Six stations are sampled at both high and low tide and reported as separate rows. Tidal phase is carried per sample and must not be averaged away - it is the only such pairing on the platform.

provenance.note: Adi Ganga returns dissolved oxygen of NIL at multiple stations; that is the upstream's own value, not a missing reading.

source: West Bengal Pollution Control Board, EMIS Water Quality Information System
notes: The Adi Ganga is sampled at six points, each SEPARATELY at high tide and low tide - the only tidal station pairing on this platform. High- and low-tide readings are kept apart rather than averaged, because the same location is a different water body six hours apart. 'NIL' dissolved oxygen is stored as 0.0: it is a real measurement, not a missing value.
coords_note: WBPCB publishes no station coordinates. Positions are hand-placed from station names against the mapped channel and flagged coords_approximate; stations we could not place carry null coordinates rather than a guess.

rivers.name: Adi Ganga
rivers.cpcb_class: Not on the CPCB national polluted-stretch list; WBPCB Use-Based Class E
rivers.description: The original course of the Ganga through south Kolkata, past Kalighat, now largely the engineered channel also called Tolly's Nullah. Sampled at six points, each separately at high and low tide.
rivers.notes: Dissolved oxygen is NIL at every monitored point in the latest round and low tide runs worse than high - less dilution, more concentration.

rivers.name: Groundwater monitoring
rivers.unmapped_note: 15 station(s) have readings but no coordinates: WBPCB publishes none and we do not guess. Their series are retained here.
rivers.description: WBPCB groundwater monitoring points, sampled under the same programme.
rivers.notes: Groundwater samples carry no DO or BOD - a different parameter set from the river stations.

rivers.description: The Ganga distributary Kolkata was built on and draws essentially all its drinking water from, abstracted at Palta about 22 km north and at Garden Reach. Tidal this far inland.
rivers.notes: Comparatively healthy at the intakes; the pollution story is the Adi Ganga, not the mainstem.
